title: Pricing Desk Note: Usage Scaling of Residential Electricity Supply Renewal Reductions
content:
**Rule.** On a Residential Electricity Supply renewal, the combined reduction on the renewal rate (the per-kWh renewal reductions added together into one figure) is scaled by the agreement's average consumption. The average is the kWh of the agreement's energy charge lines whose billing cycle started less than twelve whole months before the election date, added up and divided by the number of those energy charge lines. At an average of 1,000 kWh or more the combined reduction is multiplied by the high-volume factor of 1.4, from 800 up to but not including 1,000 kWh by the mid-volume factor of 1.2, and below 800 kWh it is taken as it stands. An agreement with no such lines takes the combined reduction as it stands.

| Average kWh per energy charge line | Combined reduction is |
|---|---|
| 1,000 or more | multiplied by 1.4 |
| 800 up to but not including 1,000 | multiplied by 1.2 |
| below 800 | taken as it stands |

**Boundaries.** An average of exactly 1,000 kWh takes 1.4 and 999.5 kWh takes 1.2; exactly 800 kWh takes 1.2 and 799.5 kWh takes the reduction as it stands.

**Example (hypothetical).** A combined reduction of 0.55 cents per kWh on an agreement averaging 1,040 kWh becomes 0.55 multiplied by 1.4, which is 0.77 cents per kWh. On a time-of-use agreement the on-peak and off-peak lines are each counted as one line in the average.
